additions.reasoning: The text explicitly states that sadness (עצבות) and its offspring derive from the domem (earth/mineral) element. In section 8, the night-walking parable is introduced with the parable of someone 'fearing thorns, pits, evil beasts, and bandits' — and the analysis maps these to the four elements' bad middot. While פחתים (pits) is in the dataset as a bechina of דומם, the actual bad middah it produces (עצבות, sadness) is not represented as a bechina node for Torah #4. The text says: 'עצבות ותולדותיהן נמשכין מדומם' — sadness derives from domem. This בחינת relationship belongs in Package 6 (evil elements). Suggested edge: עצבות ↔ דומם (bechina).

The text explicitly states that evil desires (תאוות רעות) and their offspring derive from the tzomea'ch (plant) element. While קוצים (thorns) is in the dataset as a bechina of צומח, the actual bad middah (תאוות רעות) is not represented as a bechina node for Torah #4. The relationship is the same structural pattern as: דברים בטלים ↔ חי and גאוה ↔ מדבר. The missing edge: תאוות רעות ↔ צומח (bechina).

additions.concept: ארץ מצרים / גלות (Egypt/Exile as Evil Kingdom)
additions.reasoning: The text repeatedly describes the exile of malkhut 'among the nations' (העכו"ם) as the fundamental problem. The phrase 'ארץ מצרים' and 'גלות' are used as bechinot of the exile-state of malkhut. The verse 'אשר הוצאתיך מארץ מצרים מבית עבדים' is parsed: Egypt = the nations who oppress (מצרים = מצרים = those who constrain), 'מבית עבדים' = slavery to the four evil middot. These concepts describe the evil state of malkhut in exile. Suggested edges: ארץ מצרים ↔ מלכות בגלות (bechina), or מצרים ↔ עכו"ם (bechina).

additions.source_quote: וְהָיָה מְדַבֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּאוֹר אֵין סוֹף, אֲבָל הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הָיָה בִּבְחִינַת: וְהַחַיּוֹת רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב
additions.reasoning: The concept of 'ratzo vaShov' (running and returning, from Ezekiel's vision of the living creatures) is central to Torah #4's teaching on cleaving to Ein Sof. Moshe's hitpashetut (dissolution into the Infinite) had to be in the mode of ratzo vaShov — complete immersion followed by return to the world. This is described as a bechina: the tzaddik's cleaving to Ein Sof is a bechina of 'ratzo vaShov.' No bechina edges for Torah #4 capture this. Suggested edge: התפשטות הגשמיות ↔ רצוא ושוב (bechina) or רצוא ושוב ↔ אין סוף (bechina).

additions.concept: הִסְתַּלְּקוּת משֶׁה בְּשַׁבָּת בְּשַׁעְתָּא דְּמִנְחָה (Moses's departure on Shabbat at Mincha)
additions.source_quote: שֶׁהִסְתַּלְּקוּת מֹשֶׁה בְּשַׁבָּת בְּשַׁעְתָּא דְּמִנְחָה, שֶׁאָז הִתְגַּלּוּת רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין
additions.reasoning: The Zohar's teaching that Moshe departed on Shabbat at the time of Mincha prayer — when the 'ra'ava de-ra'avin' (will of all wills / ratsón ein sof) is revealed — is cited as a bechina: Moshe's departure IS the moment of highest Ein Sof revelation because Moshe annihilated his yesh (existence). This is a specific bechina of the Ein Sof cluster (Package 3) not captured in the dataset.

additions.concept: צֵרוּפֵי אוֹתִיּוֹת / צֵרוּפִים רָעִים (Letter-Combinations / Evil Permutations)
additions.source_quote: וְכָל עֲבֵרָה יֵשׁ לָהּ צֵרוּף אוֹתִיּוֹת. וּכְשֶׁעָבַר אֵיזֶה עֲבֵרָה, אֲזַי נֶחְקָק צֵרוּף רַע עַל עַצְמוֹתָיו
additions.reasoning: The concept of 'tziruf otiyot' (letter-permutations/combinations) is central to the sin-mechanism in Torah #4: every sin has a letter-combination, and transgressing engraves an evil permutation on one's bones. The good letter-combination is destroyed and an evil one is built. Since מלכות = אותיות (letters/speech), and 'צרוף רע' represents the corruption of speech/malkhut, this belongs in Package 1. The bechina relationship: צרוף רע ↔ חטא/עברה, or עצמות ↔ צרוף אותיות. Some related eitza edges exist in the dataset but the bechina aspect (what evil letter-combinations essentially ARE) is underdeveloped.

additions.concept: עֲנָוָה / שִׂים עַצְמוֹ כְּשִׁירַיִם (Humility / Making Oneself as Leftovers)
additions.source_quote: וְהַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה, שֶׁמֵּשִׂים עַצְמוֹ כְּשִׁירַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה עָנָו מְאֹד
additions.reasoning: Humility (ענוה) and 'making oneself as leftovers' (שים עצמו כשירים) are described as the essential quality of the talmid chakham/Moshe that gives him the power to atone. The text explicitly states: 'כי זה מן הנמנע שלא יבוא לאדם איזה גדלות' — when praised, inevitably pride comes. But Moshe was 'עָנָו מְאֹד' (very humble), and this IS what made him capable of atonement. The bechina: ענוה ↔ כח לכפר (humility = power to atone), or ענוה ↔ חכמה מאין תמצא. This connects the משה/אין cluster to ענוה as its defining quality. Missing bechina edge for reference=4.

analysis_notes.note_on_duplicates: Edges 1030 and 1031 represent the same bechina (מיתה ↔ ודוי דברים) with slightly different node text (מִּיתָה vs מֵתָה — different grammatical forms from the same Aramaic story). Both counted; nodes normalized to single 'מיתה' node in the package.
analysis_notes.note_on_null_id_edges: Two edges with null IDs were found and confirmed as Torah #4 bechina: (1) גרבי דמשחא ↔ דעת and (2) יום המיתה ↔ ודוי דברים. Both are legitimate bechina statements from the source text.
